name: contentmaschine.ai API
description:
External REST API for contentmaschine.ai.

## Authentication
All `/v1/*` endpoints require an API key sent as a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-cm-<your-key>
```
Manage your API key in the Dashboard → API tab.

## Scopes
Each operation names the scope it needs in `x-required-scope`. There are five
containers (`images`, `videos`, `audio`, `text`, `files`), each with `read` and `write`.
**A write scope always includes the read scope of the same container**: a token
with `images:write` can also call everything that needs `images:read`. The rule does
not cross containers, so `images:write` does not grant `text:read`.

## Async pattern
Image generation and upscaling are asynchronous.
1. Submit a job - receive a `job_id` (or `krea_job_id` for upscale).
2. Poll the status endpoint until `status` is `completed` or `failed`.
3. Download the result using the returned `download_url`.

## Downloading files
There are TWO download paths and they do NOT authorize the same way.

- `GET /v1/files/{uuid}/download` requires `files:read` **plus** the read
  scope of the container the file belongs to (an image needs `images:read`,
  a video `videos:read`, and so on). A token holding `files:read` alone gets
  a 404 for a file it may not read - deliberately a 404, not a 403, so a
  denial is indistinguishable from a nonexistent file.
- `GET /api/files/download/{uuid}` is the older path. It is still reachable
  with the same Bearer token and it is owner-checked. For an `sk-cm-` API key
  it carries **no scope check at all** - any valid key belonging to the owner
  is served the file. An OAuth access token needs the read scope of the
  file's container, as on the v1 route, and gets a 404 without it.
  It is documented because real callers use it. Prefer the `/v1/` route.

Both return a 302 to a presigned URL valid for one hour when the file lives
in object storage. That redirect target is a CREDENTIAL: anyone holding it
can read the object until it expires. Do not log it or pass it on.

## Errors
Every error uses ONE envelope (see the `ErrorEnvelope` schema and the
`default` response on every operation):
```json
{"success":false,"error":{"message":"...","code":404,"type":"not_found",
 "correlation_id":"0f3a...c1"},"timestamp":"2026-09-01T12:00:00+00:00"}
```
Branch on `error.type`, never on `error.message` - the sentence may be
reworded at any time. `error.code` is always the integer HTTP status.
`error.correlation_id` is the handle to quote to support: it appears in both
the response and the server log line for the same request.

## Breaking changes
Three changes have already shipped on this surface. See the machine-readable
`x-breaking-changes` block at the root of this document for the full detail.

1. **Gallery item identity moved from the generation uuid to the FILE uuid.**
   `GalleryItem.uuid` is now the uuid of the file, which is what
   `/api/files/download/{uuid}` and the v1 file routes take. The generation
   uuid is still returned, under the new `generation_uuid` field.
2. **The `category` vocabulary moved from singular to plural container names**
   (`image` -> `images`, `video` -> `videos`). Every payload now reports the
   plural, matching the scope vocabulary. The singular forms are still
   ACCEPTED on the `?category=` filter for one more release and answer with a
   `Deprecation: true` header; they will be removed.
3. **`error.code` is now always the integer HTTP status.** The three token
   failure identifiers (`token_expired`, `token_revoked`, `token_invalid`)
   used to be put in `error.code` as strings; they are byte-identical but now
   live in the new, always-present `error.type`. If you branch on
   `error.code === "token_revoked"`, rename the key.
